words.gloss: even if one leaves (i.e., does not trust)
in times of ruin or distress

literal: Even if one trusts, or even if one does not trust, in times of ruin, without trusting and without openly splitting, one should let them be.
translation: Whether you trust them or not, in times of distress, you should let them be—neither fully trusting them nor openly breaking away from them.
modern: ஒருவரை நம்பினாலும் அல்லது நம்பாவிட்டாலும், நமக்குத் துன்பம் வரும் காலத்தில், அவரை முழுமையாக நம்பாமலும் அவரிடமிருந்து முற்றிலும் பிரிந்துவிடாமலும் அப்படியே விட்டுவிட வேண்டும்.
explanation: This couplet advises how to handle doubtful allies or hidden enemies during times of distress or ruin. Even if you have trusted them in the past, or if you have always doubted them, when you face a crisis, you must exercise extreme caution. You should not place complete trust in them (தேறான்), as they might betray you, nor should you openly break ties or show enmity (பகாஅன்), as that could provoke immediate hostility. The best course of action is to maintain a safe distance and let them be (விடல்) without revealing your true stance.
